title: Asked by thalam: Each host's capabilities in the flake's `estate` output (L2's export)
body:
Each host's capabilities in the flake's `estate` output (L2's export) (graft:01a19b0c-d51b..df8b, from thalam)

What was needed:
- thalam: Beside each host's services in `nix#estate`, a `capabilities` list in the estate's vocabulary (vg-paradigms' estate/capabilities.toml: e.g. `kvm`, `cuda`, `arch:aarch64`, `os:linux`), set by the module that provides it where it's turned on (a GPU driver module adds `cuda`, KVM adds `kvm`), the way `estate.services` is. A new field in a versioned export: bump `nix#exports.version` if your rule says adding one does (your claim says adding doesn't), and say which version carries it.

Answer (done): Done in vg-dotfiles a5ac0eb: `nix#estate.<host>.capabilities`, a sorted list of distinct ids, set by the module that provides each where it's turned on (estate.nix: `nix` on every host; the Tenstorrent module: `tenstorrent`; graphics: `vulkan` with an AMD or NVIDIA driver, `opencl` with ROCm OpenCL). Today: vgkraken, vgsquid-azul, vgsquid-onyx [nix, opencl, vulkan]; vgsquid-jade [nix, tenstorrent, vulkan]; vgnixmini, vgmacbook, vgwsl2 [nix]. It ships in exports.version 1 (adding a field doesn't bump it), and exports.test.sh checks its shape. The field is always present. Only ids already in vg-paradigms' estate/capabilities.toml are used: no `rocm` or `cuda` (neither toolkit is installed), and no `kvm`, `arch:*` or `os:*` because the vocabulary doesn't have them. I've asked vg-paradigms to add them (graft 01a1c1db-427e). A todo here adds `kvm` once it exists. vgwsl2 still has no /dev/kvm (Windows 26200.9711's AMD nested-virtualization regression).
